title: Define the Principal seam and the waitlist-safe route marker
description:
**Phase 1 of 7.** Keep it small and merge it within a day: three phase-3 tasks fork from it and must agree on the shape first.

- **Blocked by:** nothing, start today
- **Runs in parallel with:** 79ca6a, 7c1382, 0ab02c, 272aea
- **Unblocks:** 5f0c4c, fac2ee, 79578e

---
Principal is a frozen dataclass with a kind (user or worker), tenant_id, and either user_id with membership status and role, or worker_id. Add the FastAPI dependency that will resolve it and the explicit marker that declares a route reachable by a waitlisted member. No resolver implementations and no enforcement in this task.

Routing is default deny by construction: a route serves an enabled member unless it is explicitly marked otherwise. Do not build a denylist of expensive routes. The next route someone adds would be open by default, and one day that route is the one that calls the model.

**Done when:** the type and the marker are merged so the three dependent tasks can proceed in parallel.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Architect ruling: the exact shape, so the three dependent tasks can fork.**

```python
class PrincipalKind(StrEnum):
    USER = "user"
    WORKER = "worker"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Principal:
    kind: PrincipalKind
    tenant_id: str
    user_id: str | None = None
    worker_id: str | None = None
    membership_status: MembershipStatus | None = None
    role: Role | None = None
```

**Two kinds, and only two.** Do not add a system, service, or test kind. A test-only principal is a second authentication path, and the repository does not keep two; our own tooling authenticates as a worker (see d71ed5).

**The marker is opt-out, not opt-in.** The dependency requires an enabled member by default. A route reachable by a waitlisted member says so explicitly. As of today exactly one route is waitlist-safe: `GET /me`. `/health` and the authentication routes take no principal at all and are not part of the marker system.

**Not in this task:** resolvers, JWT verification, worker credentials, enforcement. Land the type and the marker, nothing else. Three tasks are waiting on the shape rather than the behavior.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Review of #115. Shape is right; one type needs to go before this merges.**

The dataclass matches the ruling, `test_principal_kind_has_user_and_worker_only` encodes the two-kinds constraint as a test rather than a comment, the marker defaults to `requires_enabled_member` so it is genuinely opt-out, and `resolve_principal` is a shape-only seam with the docstring saying resolvers land later. Gherkin is first. Scope held.

**The defect: `MembershipStatus` in principal.py duplicates state that already exists and cannot represent all of it.**

#111 landed `OrganizationStatus` in models.py with `PENDING`, `ENABLED`, `SUSPENDED`. The new enum has `ENABLED` and `WAITLISTED`, which is the same concept with a different word for the same state, and it is missing the third one.

Three consequences, in order of how soon they bite:

- **A suspended organization has no representation.** b574a6 implements suspend, and a member of a suspended organization maps to neither `ENABLED` nor `WAITLISTED`. Whatever the resolver picks in 5f0c4c will be wrong, and the failure will look like an authorization bug rather than a modelling one.
- **Two words for one state.** `WAITLISTED` and `PENDING` are the same organization lifecycle state. Two vocabularies for one thing drift, and the drift shows up in whichever one a later reader does not know about.
- **The name is claimed by something else.** `Membership` on develop carries `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `role`, `joined_at` and no status. When ae51dc lands invitations, a genuine per-member status of invited, active, or removed will want exactly this name, and it will collide with a field that actually describes the organization.

**Fix: carry `OrganizationStatus` on the principal and delete the new enum.** That is the same choice already made one line above, where `Role` aliases `MemberRole` from models rather than redefining it. Enablement is an organization property; the principal reports it, it does not define its own.

`PrincipalRoutePolicy.requires_enabled_member` keeps its name and meaning, since it asks a question about the caller rather than naming a state.

Not blocking anything else: the seam's shape is what the three dependent tasks were waiting on, and this change does not move it. Python CI was still running when I looked, so this is a review note rather than a merge signal.
